flashcards.q: What are Porter's Five Forces and at what level (industry vs company) do they operate?
flashcards.a: Competitive rivalry, bargaining power of buyers, bargaining power of suppliers, threat of substitutes, threat of new entrants. They operate at the INDUSTRY level -- how much value can ANY participant in this category keep, largely independent of any one company's execution.

Scale economies, network economies, counter-positioning, switching costs, branding, cornered resources, process power -- each a distinct COMPANY-level mechanism by which a specific advantage survives contact with a competitor.

flashcards.q: Why is 'we use GPT-5 / a specific foundation model' not a moat, even for a genuinely good product?
flashcards.a: The foundation-model layer is at product stage, moving toward commodity, with multiple credible competing providers and standardizing interfaces -- a competitor can switch to or already use an equivalent model with comparable ease. Real advantage has to live in a harder-to-replicate layer: process power, switching costs, or genuinely proprietary data.

flashcards.q: How has 'cornered resources' as a moat shifted meaning in the AI era?
flashcards.a: Raw proprietary datasets are less defensible now (foundation models train on enormous public/licensed corpora), but RIGHTS-CLEARED, CONTINUOUSLY REFRESHED, genuinely proprietary data -- updated faster than a competitor could re-derive it -- remains a strong cornered resource. Scarce talent and proprietary hardware/infra access are the other live examples.

flashcards.q: Why is process power specifically underestimated by teams building 'AI wrapper' products?
flashcards.a: The visible product (prompt, UI, wrapper) is genuinely easy to copy in a weekend, which makes teams assume the whole thing is easy to replicate. But getting a system to 99%+ reliable accuracy on a mission-critical task in production requires years of unglamorous edge-case engineering and eval infrastructure that a fast-follower can't shortcut by copying only what's externally visible.

flashcards.q: Describe Wardley mapping's evolution axis and its four stages.
flashcards.a: Genesis (novel, nobody's solved it) -> Custom-Built (maturing, still scarce/differentiating) -> Product (mature, multiple vendors) -> Commodity/Utility (standardized, interchangeable, rent it). Components move rightward over time driven by competition and standardization; compute took ~40 years to go from genesis to commodity.

flashcards.q: What is the build-vs-buy rule that follows from Wardley's evolution axis?
flashcards.a: Build at genesis (nobody's solved it, may be your differentiation). Build or carefully evaluate at custom-built. BUY at product stage (multiple vendors, comparison-shop). RENT/consume as utility at commodity -- building custom here is a strategic tax with no corresponding advantage.

flashcards.q: What real-world example illustrates the cost of ignoring a component's evolution DIRECTION, not just its current stage?
flashcards.a: Banking industry: billions invested in custom-built core-banking systems roughly 2010-2020, at the same time those systems were visibly transitioning toward the product stage -- the investment fought the evolution direction instead of riding it.

flashcards.q: What two conditions should be true before platform-izing a capability, rather than keeping it as a product?
flashcards.a: Evidenced third-party demand to actually build on top of it (not a hunch), and the underlying capability is differentiated enough (not racing toward commodity) to anchor real ecosystem value -- platform-izing carries real ongoing costs (API stability, backward compatibility, third-party support).

flashcards.q: What is the honest synthesis for what constitutes a durable moat in an AI product specifically?
flashcards.a: A thin prompt or wrapper around a foundation model is not a moat -- that layer commoditizes too fast. Durable advantage comes from process power (production reliability engineering) combined with switching costs (deep workflow embedding) and, where genuinely available, cornered resources (proprietary, refreshed, rights-cleared data) -- IN COMBINATION, not any single power alone.
